answer: A real operator rarely repeats the exact same action sequence dozens of times in a row; a loop is a strong automation signal. The system watches for repeated action loops — the same three or four actions cycling — and requires a liveness challenge when a session's loop count passes a threshold, because a human would vary the sequence or stop. The system trusts a nadir only after its actions survive the consistency check. When the grove settles over the comet, the session holds because every action carried its own proof.
